question.raw: Are eggs good to eat? How many should I eat? I keep hearing they're full of cholesterol but also that they're the perfect protein. Should I just have eggs for breakfast every day?

framings.text: In healthy adults, does ~1 standard egg/day replacing a refined-carb breakfast raise heart risk?
Do 2+ eggs/day help a healthy adult feel full and lose weight?
Is one egg a day meaningful protein for building muscle?
For someone with diabetes, does adding a daily egg raise heart risk?
Do pasture-raised eggs change the heart-risk answer vs standard?
For a cholesterol hyper-responder, does a daily egg raise heart risk?

summary.verdict: No reliable link to cardiovascular events for a healthy, non-diabetic adult at ~1 egg/day. It raises LDL ~8 mg/dL — what matters is what the egg replaces.
summary.scope: healthy · non-diabetic · normolipidemic · ~1/day · hard CVD events (not LDL alone)
cruxes: Comparator — “eggs vs what?” Swapping ½ egg/day for nuts/legumes ≈ −13% mortality; for processed meat, eggs look better.
Do you trust observational adjustment? US egg-eaters eat 5× more bacon; the association’s sign flips US (harm) vs China (protective).

nodes.note: But the egg signal went NON-significant after adjusting for dietary cholesterol — it’s the cholesterol, not the egg. Self-verified against JAMA.
The main null, and the substitution engine: egg→red/processed meat = worse; egg→fish/legumes = better.
Global null across 50 countries. Rides on heavy pharma-platform funding — flagged, not disqualifying.
Sign is OPPOSITE the US cohorts, because egg intake tracks higher SES/health in China. This is the confounding fingerprint.
Hides a heart-failure signal: 1.15 (1.02–1.30) at 1/day. The graph keeps what the headline drops.
Rates its own inputs “critically low” quality (AMSTAR-2). Convergence on null ≠ a strong null — this is why confidence stays capped.

nodes.find: +½ egg/day → mortality HR 1.07; 63% mediated by cholesterol.
nodes.note: Names the comparator crux with numbers: ½ egg → nuts/legumes = −13% mortality.
INDEPENDENT (non-industry) — settles the physiology. Survives a COI-cluster ablation, so the LDL rise isn’t industry spin.

nodes.find: Only ~7% of studies adjusted for saturated fat.
nodes.note: The confounding argument is REAL — but the review is egg-industry-funded. Carry the point AND the conflict.
Quantifies the funding bias — but authored by anti-egg advocates (PCRM). Symmetric COI: neither pole gets a free pass.

nodes.find: “The noise is much stronger than the signal.”
nodes.note: Undercuts confident causal claims on BOTH sides — a calibration anchor for how much any single cohort can carry.
